purpose: for attaining bodhi (bodhi saṃlabdhahetoḥ); merit for the donors (etat puṇyānubhāvena phalaṃ prāptotu)
notes: Chronograms: 'nabha-nayana-nava' = 0-2-9 → NS 920, which matches 'samvat 920'. The inserted verse <<...>> ('gagana ca nayana randhra') also gives 920. That verse, however, has 'śuke māse' (perhaps śuci, i.e. Āṣāḍha/Jyeṣṭha) and 'vāsare sūryyaputre' (Saturday), which conflict with the main colophon (Śrāvaṇa, bhumiputra/aṅgāravāra = Tuesday). It may be a rejected first draft. NS 920 Śrāvaṇa śukla 1 falls around 22 July 1800, which was a Tuesday, so it fits the main colophon. The catalogue lists 'Vajrācārya Śripati' as a third scribe. But 'śrepateya' carries the Newari genitive -ya, and only Bhājupati and Bhājudeva carry the Sanskrit instrumental of agency. So they are probably Śrīpati's sons and the actual scribes, though the son relation is inferred. The verse says Matyaṅa made the book, while the Newari prose names his three sons as dānapati. Matyaṅa is therefore marked commissioner with medium confidence.
